scope: Bound manual backup encryption and release both panel and application operation locks
behavior: Manual file export and browser-copy creation have a three-minute encryption deadline. Password and confirmation survive timeout for explicit retry.
Both RecoveryPanel and App bound their encryption waits. The App finally releases its busy lock on expiry and checks component generation before updating UI.
A late encryption result cannot start download/storage or unlock a newer operation. Already-running WebCrypto is not cancelled.
Storage writes after successful encryption retain their existing independent storage deadlines and uncertain-commit semantics.

unit.scope: Two new component cases expire file/browser encryption, retain inputs and reject an old result during a pending explicit retry, plus existing panel/inspection cases.

browserDiscovery.finding: The first panel-only fix showed timeout but App still held its outer fieldset disabled while awaiting encryption. Real browser tests exposed the unreleased application operation lock; App was then bounded too.

browserRuns.scope: Four new real-browser PBKDF2/AES cases plus two offline inspection cases. The additional requested recovery-browser.spec.ts pattern matched no file; the actual browser-copy regression was run separately.
Existing desktop/mobile browser-copy reload, quota failure and selected-copy removal.

release.scope: Normal web build/typecheck and release gate after the final browser run.

limits: Browser deadline tests use real crypto with the first derived-key result held and a virtual clock; they do not simulate physical suspend or terminate WebCrypto.
No full regression, runtime refresh, native-wallet ceremony or public deployment.
Automatic autosave encryption and already-started storage writes are outside this manual export deadline.
